thread:
sara_support: FYI incoming from AcmeCo — they've got an API key visible in the console but their requests are getting 401. Customer says key 'sk-acme-01' was created during onboarding.
provision-bot: provisioning job #pv-8421 completed for tenant acmeco at 2026-03-16T18:12:03Z. service-account: sa-acme-8421 created. claim: queued.
mike_onboard: I repro'd quickly — console shows key, but calling /v1/models returns 401. curl attached below.
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/completions \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-01" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"hi"}' \n  -i
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"unauthorized","reason":"key_not_bound_to_project","request_id":"req_0abc"}
```
provision-bot: note: provisioning step 'attach-claim' returned status SUCCESS (exit_code 0) — timestamped logs show claim job finished but no explicit project_id in binding metadata.
elaine_se: sounds like the claim binding didn't attach the project_id on the service account token. I've seen this happen if the OIDC claim arrives before the claim-watcher picks it up (race). The key token exists, but our auth layer rejects because lookup->project mapping is empty.
sara_support: customer provided logs showing key present in console: Key ID sk-acme-01  created at 2026-03-16T18:11:59Z. They tried in dev and prod; same 401.
mike_onboard: quick internal check:
```bash
# admin inspect command (internal)
redwood-admin inspect-key sk-acme-01 --json
{
  "key":"sk-acme-01",
  "status":"active",
  "service_account":"sa-acme-8421",
  "project": null,
  "scopes": ["completions","embeddings"]
}
```
elaine_se: yep project == null is the root cause. auth middleware requires project for scoping and billing.
julia_security: curious if this could be elevated to a security incident (unbound keys). If someone reuses the key anywhere else it won't map — but it's failing closed (401) so not a leak. Still want audit: who/what created the service account and why binding missing.
ops_martin: I dug into provisioner logs. The sequence: create-sa -> emit-claim -> provisioner returns 0 -> provision-bot marks job success. The claim-watcher job that applies the project label runs on a separate daemon and may have processed backlog. There's a 20s window where API will be unhappy. We need a guard.
sara_support: Customer impact: they can't integrate now and are blocked on first-API-call test. They asked for an immediate fix.
mike_onboard: Temporary fix: rebind the key to the correct project from support console. I did: `Support Console -> Tenants -> acmeco -> Keys -> sk-acme-01 -> Rebind to acmeco-prod` and then validated.
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/completions \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-01" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"hello"}' \n  -i
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":"resp_0def","model":"redwood-small","output":"Hi!"}
```
sara_support: Customer confirmed success after rebind, thanks. They asked what caused it and whether it will happen again.
elaine_se: Root cause: provisioning race between the provisioner marking job success and the claim-watcher applying project labels. The provisioner assumed asynchronous claim application would always complete quickly. Sometimes the label apply lags and our auth-lookups see null project.
julia_security: Recommendation: treat unbound keys as failed provisioning (don't return success) and add an audit event when service_account.project == null.
ops_martin: Proposed short-term mitigations:
- Make support rebind quick path (done).
- Add a probe that runs post-provision: `inspect-key` and fails job if project==null (30s timeout, 3 retries).
- Emit clearer logs (provisioner: claim-apply: pending) so provisioning UI shows "waiting on claim-watcher" instead of success.
- Create alert if >1% of onboard jobs have project==null in provisioning window.
mike_onboard: I'll push a small change to provisioner to wait up to 30s for claim-watcher (with exponential backoff) and surface failure if still unbound. Assigning to @ops_martin for triage and to @elaine_se for review.
ops_martin: I'll own rollout and the alert. I'll also add a one-time migration job to scan last 48h for keys with null project and rebind automatically.
julia_security: please include a note in the postmortem that keys must never be left in limbo; we need an event for compliance.
sara_support: Filed support ticket to AcmeCo with update and ETA for fix. Customer happy for now since rebind worked, but they'd like confirm when permanent fix lands. :thumbsup:
mike_onboard: PR reference: github.com/redwood/provisioner/pull/241 — adds post-provision inspect step. ETA for rollout: today -> canary in us-west then global tomorrow.
ops_martin: I'll run scan now and post results.
provision-bot: scheduled job #scan-keys-48h started.
elaine_se: follow-up: once we have the guardrail, let's also surface a clearer error to customers when request fails due to unbound key (401 + reason: key_not_bound_to_project, docs link).
sara_support: noted. closing thread once migration completes.
